def stamp_sdk_method_name!(op, method, path)
  entry = SDK_METHOD_NAMES[[method.to_s, path.to_s]]
  return unless entry

  op["x-fern-sdk-group-name"] = entry[:group]
  op["x-fern-sdk-method-name"] = entry[:name]
end

# Resolve a parameter's field ("in", "name", ...) whether the parameter is
# inline or a $ref into #/components/parameters. params_components is the merged
# @components["parameters"] map (keyed by ref tail). Returns nil when it cannot
# be resolved so callers can fall back to their inline handling.
def resolve_param_field(param, params_components, field)
  return param[field] if param.is_a?(Hash) && param.key?(field)

  ref = param.is_a?(Hash) ? param["$ref"].to_s : ""
  return nil unless ref.start_with?("#/components/parameters/")

  tail = ref.split("/").last
  comp = params_components.is_a?(Hash) ? params_components[tail] : nil
  comp.is_a?(Hash) ? comp[field] : nil
end

def ensure_path_parameters!(op, path, params_components = {})
  wanted = path.scan(/\{([^}]+)\}/).flatten
  existing = Array(op["parameters"]).select do |param|
    # Keep a $ref to a NON-path parameter (query/header/cookie: start/end, page,
    # page-size, sort-order, ...). The old predicate resolved a $ref to its
    # ref-tail name, which never matches a {path} placeholder, so every $ref
    # query param was silently pruned (then GC'd by prune_components). Inline
    # params and $ref PATH params keep the original name test below.
    if param.is_a?(Hash) && param["$ref"].is_a?(String)
      resolved_in = resolve_param_field(param, params_components, "in")
      next true if resolved_in && resolved_in != "path"
    end
    name = parameter_name(param)
    name.nil? || wanted.include?(name)
  end
  seen = existing.each_with_object(Set.new) do |param, set|
    name = parameter_name(param)
    next unless name

    set << name
  end
  wanted.each do |name|
    next if seen.include?(name)

    existing << {
      "name" => name,
      "in" => "path",
      "required" => true,
      "schema" => {"type" => "string"}
    }
    seen << name
  end
  op["parameters"] = existing unless existing.empty?
end

def json_pointer_exists?(doc, ref)
  return false unless ref.start_with?("#/")

  current = doc
  ref.sub("#/", "").split("/").each do |raw|
    token = raw.gsub("~1", "/").gsub("~0", "~")
    return false unless current.is_a?(Hash) && current.key?(token)

    current = current[token]
  end
  true
end

class Merger
  attr_reader :quarantine

  def initialize(options)
    @options = options
    @operations = {}
    @components = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = {} }
    @component_hashes = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = {} }
    @quarantine = []
    @used_operation_ids = Set.new
    @aliases = Set.new
    @security_header_aliases = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = Set.new }
  end

  def add_yaml_file(path, kind)
    doc = load_yaml_file(path)
    return unless doc.is_a?(Hash)

    label = source_label(path, @options)
    domain = domain_from_path(path)
    servers = Array(doc["servers"]).map { |server| server["url"].to_s }
    security_schemes = doc.dig("components", "securitySchemes") || {}
    collect_security_aliases(security_schemes)
    ref_maps = merge_components(doc["components"] || {}, domain)
    Array(doc.dig("components", "securitySchemes")).each { |scheme| @aliases << scheme[0].to_s if scheme[0].to_s != "ApiKeyAuth" }

    paths = doc["paths"] || {}
    paths.keys.sort.each do |raw_path|
      item = paths[raw_path]
      next unless item.is_a?(Hash)

      inherited_parameters = Array(item["parameters"])
      item.keys.map(&:to_s).select { |m| METHODS.include?(m.downcase) }.sort_by { |m| METHOD_ORDER.fetch(m.downcase, 99) }.each do |method|
        op = deep_copy(item[method])
        op["parameters"] = merge_parameters(inherited_parameters, Array(op["parameters"]))
        aliases = operation_security_aliases(op, security_schemes)
        op["x-clockify-security-aliases"] = aliases unless aliases.empty?
        rewrite_refs!(op, ref_maps)
        normalize_security!(op, @aliases)
        normalized = normalize_path(raw_path)
        host = host_for(normalized, op, servers)
        add_operation(
          method.downcase,
          normalized,
          op,
          source: label,
          domain: domain,
          host: host,
          evidence: kind,
          priority: SOURCE_PRIORITIES.fetch(kind, 0)
        )
      end
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    reason = if defined?(Psych::SyntaxError) && e.is_a?(Psych::SyntaxError)
               "invalid YAML source quarantined"
             else
               e.message.lines.first.to_s.strip.gsub(File.expand_path(path), source_label(path, @options))
             end
    @quarantine << {
      "source" => source_label(path, @options),
      "reason" => reason
    }
  end

  def add_markdown_doc(path)
    label = source_label(path, @options)
    domain = domain_from_path(path)
    method_path_from_doc(File.readlines(path, chomp: true)).each do |method, normalized|
      op = {
        "tags" => [tag_for_domain(domain)],
        "summary" => "Documented #{method.upcase} #{normalized}",
        "description" => "Operation discovered from pasted Clockify API Markdown. Schemas stay broad unless a parsed OpenAPI source or live fixture provides narrower structure.",
        "operationId" => operation_id(method, normalized, @used_operation_ids),
        "security" => [{"ApiKeyAuth" => []}, {"AddonTokenAuth" => []}],
        "responses" => {
          "default" => {
            "description" => "Documented Clockify response.",
            "content" => {
              "application/json" => {
                "schema" => {"type" => "object", "additionalProperties" => true}
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      add_operation(
        method,
        normalized,
        op,
        source: label,
        domain: domain,
        host: host_for(normalized, op, []),
        evidence: "doc-md",
        priority: SOURCE_PRIORITIES.fetch("doc-md")
      )
    end
  end

  def apply_metadata(findings, mcp_mapping, tool_risks, tool_meta)
    @operations.each do |(method, path), record|
      op = record[:op]
      findings_for_op = Array(findings[[method, path, record[:host]]]) + Array(findings[[method, path, nil]])
      other_host_findings = findings.each_with_object([]) do |((f_method, f_path, f_host), values), out|
        next unless f_method == method && f_path == path && f_host && f_host != record[:host]

        out.concat(values)
      end
      evidence = Array(op["x-clockify-evidence"])
      source_files = Array(op["x-clockify-source-files"])
      source_live_status = op["x-clockify-live-status"].to_s
      findings_for_op.each do |finding|
        evidence << finding["bucket"]
        source_files << finding["source"]
      end
      live_status = choose_live_status(evidence, findings_for_op, [source_live_status])
      tools = Array(mcp_mapping[[method, path]]).sort
      evidence.concat(tools.flat_map { |tool| Array(tool_meta.dig(tool, "evidence")) })
      tool_statuses = tools.flat_map { |tool| Array(tool_meta.dig(tool, "statuses")) }
      live_status = choose_live_status(evidence, findings_for_op, [source_live_status] + tool_statuses)
      risk = tools.flat_map { |tool| tool_risks[tool] }.compact
      risk = Array(op["x-clockify-risk"]) if risk.empty? && Array(op["x-clockify-risk"]).any?
      risk = default_risk_for(method) if risk.empty?

      op["x-clockify-source-files"] = source_files.uniq.sort
      op["x-clockify-host"] = record[:host]
      op["x-clockify-evidence"] = evidence.uniq.sort
      op["x-clockify-live-status"] = live_status
      op["x-clockify-mcp-tools"] = tools
      op["x-clockify-risk"] = risk.uniq.sort

      raw_notes = raw_unit_notes(path)
      op["x-clockify-raw-unit-notes"] = raw_notes unless raw_notes.empty?
      notes = Array(op["x-clockify-notes"]) + quirk_notes(path, method)
      notes.concat(findings_for_op.map { |finding| finding["note"] }) if findings_for_op.any?
      notes.concat(other_host_findings.map { |finding| "Wrong-host finding not applied to live status: #{finding["note"]}" }) if other_host_findings.any?
      notes.concat(tools.flat_map { |tool| Array(tool_meta.dig(tool, "notes")) }) if tools.any?
      op["x-clockify-notes"] = notes.uniq.sort unless notes.empty?
      ensure_path_parameters!(op, path, @components["parameters"])
      normalize_op_tags!(op)
      stamp_path_param_patterns!(op)
      ensure_pagination!(op, method, path, @components["parameters"])
      stamp_last_page_header!(op, method, path)
      stamp_sdk_method_name!(op, method, path)
      op["security"] = [{"ApiKeyAuth" => []}, {"AddonTokenAuth" => []}]
      op["servers"] = [{"url" => record[:host]}] if record[:host] != MAIN_SERVER
    end
  end

  def document
    paths = {}
    @operations.keys.sort_by { |method, path| [path, METHOD_ORDER.fetch(method, 99)] }.each do |method, path|
      paths[path] ||= {}
      paths[path][method] = sort_operation(@operations[[method, path]][:op])
    end

    doc = {
      "openapi" => "3.0.3",
      "info" => {
        "title" => "Clockify Unified OpenAPI",
        "version" => "2026-05-12",
        "description" => [
          "Generated by scripts/gen-clockify-openapi from realOPENAPI, clockify-api-probe-lab, AIII/openapi.yaml, GOCLMCP coverage docs, and QA findings.",
          "Do not edit this file by hand; run `make gen-openapi` after source evidence changes.",
          "Operation vendor extensions preserve provenance, host, live status, MCP mapping, risk, raw unit notes, and known upstream quirks."
        ].join("\n")
      },
      "servers" => [
        {"url" => MAIN_SERVER, "description" => "Main Clockify API"},
        {"url" => REPORTS_SERVER, "description" => "Clockify reports and shared-reports API"},
        {"url" => AUDIT_LOG_SERVER, "description" => "Clockify audit-log API"}
      ],
      "security" => [{"ApiKeyAuth" => []}],
      "tags" => tags(paths),
      "paths" => paths,
      "components" => pruned_components(paths),
      "x-clockify-generation" => {
        "generator" => "scripts/gen-clockify-openapi",
        "sourceManifest" => @options[:source_manifest],
        "sourcePrecedence" => [
          "live/probe findings metadata",
          "realOPENAPI operation bodies",
          "probe-lab OpenAPI operation bodies",
          "probe-lab fragments/supplementary OpenAPI operation bodies",
          "AIII official-style OpenAPI export operation bodies for otherwise-missing gaps",
          "pasted DOC Markdown operation inventory",
          "GOCLMCP catalog/coverage annotations"
        ],
        "securityAliasesNormalized" => @aliases.to_a.uniq.sort - ["ApiKeyAuth", "AddonTokenAuth"],
        "securityHeaderAliasesNormalized" => security_header_aliases
      },
      # Sort by both source and reason so multiple quarantines from the
       # same source file (e.g. the 3 phantom /policies/{policyId}/requests
       # routes all hitting time-off-b.yaml) land in a deterministic
       # total order. Without the secondary key the filesystem readdir
       # ordering bleeds through and the openapi-drift gate flips between
       # macOS local + Linux CI (#137 CI repro 2026-05-25).
      "x-clockify-source-quarantine" => @quarantine.sort_by { |entry| [entry["source"], entry["reason"]] }
    }
    doc
  end

  private

  def collect_security_aliases(schemes)
    return unless schemes.is_a?(Hash)

    schemes.each do |scheme, cfg|
      canonical = case scheme.to_s
                  when "AddonKeyAuth", "MarketplaceKeyAuth"
                    @aliases << scheme.to_s
                    "AddonTokenAuth"
                  when "ApiKeyAuth"
                    "ApiKeyAuth"
                  else
                    scheme.to_s
                  end
      header = cfg.is_a?(Hash) ? cfg["name"].to_s : ""
      @security_header_aliases[canonical] << header unless header.empty?
    end
  end

  def security_header_aliases
    @security_header_aliases.keys.sort.each_with_object({}) do |scheme, out|
      out[scheme] = @security_header_aliases[scheme].to_a.sort
    end
  end

  def merge_components(components, domain)
    ref_maps = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = {} }
    components.each do |section, values|
      next if section.to_s == "securitySchemes"
      next unless values.is_a?(Hash)

      values.keys.sort.each do |name|
        value = deep_copy(values[name])
        normalize_security!(value, @aliases)
        hash = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(canonical_json(value))
        existing_by_hash = @component_hashes[section][hash]
        if existing_by_hash
          ref_maps[section][name] = existing_by_hash
          next
        end

        target = name
        if @components[section].key?(target)
          prefix = pascal_domain(domain)
          target = "#{prefix}#{name}"
          suffix = 2
          while @components[section].key?(target)
            target = "#{prefix}#{name}#{suffix}"
            suffix += 1
          end
        end
        @components[section][target] = value
        @component_hashes[section][hash] = target
        ref_maps[section][name] = target
      end
    end
    ref_maps.each do |section, mapping|
      mapping.each_value do |target|
        rewrite_refs!(@components[section][target], ref_maps) if @components[section][target]
      end
    end
    ref_maps
  end

  def merge_parameters(path_params, op_params)
    # NOTE: do NOT use `path_params.concat(op_params)` here — Array#concat
    # mutates the receiver in place. `path_params` is captured once per
    # path-item by the caller and reused across every operation under
    # that path; mutating it leaked the previous method's query params
    # onto the next method, producing duplicate-identifier interfaces
    # in Fern's TS SDK output for POST/PATCH operations that shared a
    # path with a GET (e.g. POST /tags inherited GET /tags's `name`
    # query param even though probe-lab's POST defined no query params).
    # The non-destructive `+` operator avoids the leak.
    merged = []
    seen = Set.new
    (path_params + op_params).each do |param|
      key = if param.is_a?(Hash) && param["$ref"]
              param["$ref"]
            elsif param.is_a?(Hash)
              "#{param["in"]}:#{param["name"]}"
            else
              param.to_s
            end
      next if seen.include?(key)

      seen << key
      merged << param
    end
    merged
  end

  def add_operation(method, path, op, source:, domain:, host:, evidence:, priority:)
    if phantom_path?(method, path)
      @quarantine << {
        "source" => source,
        "reason" => "phantom path quarantined (#{method.upcase} #{path}): see PHANTOM_PATHS in scripts/gen-clockify-openapi"
      }
      return
    end
    op = deep_copy(op)
    source_evidence = Array(op["x-clockify-evidence"])
    source_live_status = op["x-clockify-live-status"].to_s
    op["operationId"] = operation_id(method, path, @used_operation_ids) if op["operationId"].to_s.empty?
    op["tags"] = [tag_for_domain(domain)] if Array(op["tags"]).empty?
    op["x-clockify-source-files"] = [source]
    op["x-clockify-host"] = host
    op["x-clockify-evidence"] = ([evidence] + source_evidence).uniq.sort
    op["x-clockify-live-status"] = source_live_status.empty? ? (evidence == "real-openapi" ? "documented" : evidence) : source_live_status

    key = [method, path]
    existing = @operations[key]
    if existing.nil? || priority > existing[:priority]
      if existing
        op["x-clockify-source-files"] = (Array(op["x-clockify-source-files"]) + Array(existing[:op]["x-clockify-source-files"])).uniq.sort
        op["x-clockify-evidence"] = (Array(op["x-clockify-evidence"]) + Array(existing[:op]["x-clockify-evidence"])).uniq.sort
      end
      @operations[key] = {op: op, priority: priority, host: host}
    else
      existing[:op]["x-clockify-source-files"] = (Array(existing[:op]["x-clockify-source-files"]) + [source]).uniq.sort
      existing[:op]["x-clockify-evidence"] = (Array(existing[:op]["x-clockify-evidence"]) + [evidence]).uniq.sort
      existing[:host] = REPORTS_SERVER if host == REPORTS_SERVER
    end
  end

  def choose_live_status(evidence, findings, tool_statuses = [])
    buckets = findings.map { |finding| finding["bucket"] }
    buckets.concat(tool_statuses)
    return "live-success" if buckets.include?("live-success")
    return "workspace-state-limited" if buckets.include?("workspace-state-limited")
    return "permission-gated" if buckets.include?("permission-gated")
    # A wrong-verb 405 is as unsupported as an absent path for callers; the
    # separate bucket exists so evidence readers can tell the two apart.
    return "unsupported" if buckets.include?("unsupported") || buckets.include?("method-not-allowed")
    return "unit-only" if buckets.include?("unit-only")
    return "probe-documented" if evidence.any? { |entry| entry.to_s.start_with?("probe") }

    "documented"
  end

  def sort_operation(op)
    preferred = %w[tags summary description operationId servers security parameters requestBody responses]
    out = {}
    preferred.each { |key| out[key] = sort_deep(op[key]) if op.key?(key) }
    op.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.each do |key|
      next if out.key?(key)

      out[key] = sort_deep(op[key])
    end
    out
  end

  def tag_for_domain(domain)
    {
      "custom_fields" => "Custom Fields",
      "time_entries" => "Time Entries",
      "time_off" => "Time Off",
      "user_groups" => "User Groups"
    }.fetch(domain, domain.split(/[^a-z0-9]+/).map { |part| part[0].upcase + part[1..] }.join(" "))
  end

  def tags(paths)
    names = paths.values.flat_map do |item|
      item.values.flat_map { |op| Array(op["tags"]) }
    end.uniq.sort
    names.map { |name| {"name" => name} }
  end

  def pruned_components(paths)
    refs = Set.new
    collect_refs(paths, refs)
    changed = true
    while changed
      changed = false
      refs.to_a.each do |ref|
        match = ref.match(%r{\A#/components/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z})
        next unless match

        value = @components.dig(match[1], match[2])
        next unless value

        before = refs.size
        collect_refs(value, refs)
        changed ||= refs.size > before
      end
    end

    out = {
      "securitySchemes" => {
        "ApiKeyAuth" => {"type" => "apiKey", "in" => "header", "name" => "X-Api-Key"},
        "AddonTokenAuth" => {"type" => "apiKey", "in" => "header", "name" => "X-Addon-Token"}
      }
    }
    @components.keys.sort.each do |section|
      kept = {}
      @components[section].keys.sort.each do |name|
        ref = "#/components/#{section}/#{name}"
        kept[name] = sort_deep(@components[section][name]) if refs.include?(ref)
      end
      out[section] = kept unless kept.empty?
    end
    out
  end

  def collect_refs(value, refs)
    case value
    when Hash
      refs << value["$ref"] if value["$ref"].is_a?(String)
      value.each_value { |child| collect_refs(child, refs) }
    when Array
      value.each { |child| collect_refs(child, refs) }
    end
  end
end

def raw_allowlist_required?(op)
  host = op["x-clockify-host"].to_s
  host.empty? || host == MAIN_SERVER || host == REPORTS_SERVER
end

def document_operation_keys(doc, raw_allowlist_required_only: false)
  keys = []
  (doc["paths"] || {}).each do |path, item|
    item.each do |method, op|
      next unless METHODS.include?(method)
      next if raw_allowlist_required_only && !raw_allowlist_required?(op)

      keys << "#{method.upcase} #{normalize_path(path)}"
    end
  end
  keys.uniq.sort
end

def mcp_probe_allowlist_keys(repo_root)
  path = File.join(repo_root, "internal/tools/tier2_probe_lab_api_gen.go")
  return nil unless File.exist?(path)

  verbs = {
    "Get" => "GET",
    "Post" => "POST",
    "Put" => "PUT",
    "Patch" => "PATCH",
    "Delete" => "DELETE"
  }
  File.read(path).scan(/Method:\s+http\.Method(\w+),\s+Path:\s+"([^"]+)"/m).map do |method, raw_path|
    verb = verbs.fetch(method)
    "#{verb} #{normalize_path(raw_path)}"
  end.uniq.sort
end

def validate_document(doc, repo_root = nil)
  errors = []
  paths = doc["paths"] || {}
  operation_ids = {}
  components = doc["components"] || {}
  refs = []
  collect = lambda do |value|
    case value
    when Hash
      refs << value["$ref"] if value["$ref"].is_a?(String)
      value.each_value { |child| collect.call(child) }
    when Array
      value.each { |child| collect.call(child) }
    end
  end
  collect.call(paths)
  collect.call(components)

  refs.uniq.each { |ref| errors << "unresolved ref #{ref}" if ref.start_with?("#/") && !json_pointer_exists?(doc, ref) }

  CORE_ENTITY_REQUIRED_FIELDS.each do |schema_name, fields|
    schema = components.dig("schemas", schema_name)
    if !schema.is_a?(Hash)
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} missing"
      next
    end
    props = schema["properties"]
    required = schema["required"]
    if !props.is_a?(Hash)
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} missing properties"
      next
    end
    if !required.is_a?(Array) || required.empty?
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} must declare a non-empty required[]"
      next
    end
    fields.each do |field|
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} missing property #{field}" unless props.key?(field)
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} required[] missing #{field}" unless required.include?(field)
    end
  end

  paths.each do |path, item|
    item.each do |method, op|
      next unless METHODS.include?(method)

      id = op["operationId"].to_s
      errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing operationId" if id.empty?
      errors << "duplicate operationId #{id}" if operation_ids.key?(id)
      operation_ids[id] = true
      errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing security" if Array(op["security"]).empty?
      expected_params = path.scan(/\{([^}]+)\}/).flatten
      actual_params = Array(op["parameters"]).map do |param|
        next nil unless param.is_a?(Hash)
        next param["name"] if param["in"] == "path"

        ref = param["$ref"]
        if ref&.start_with?("#/components/parameters/")
          components.dig("parameters", ref.split("/").last, "name")
        end
      end.compact
      expected_params.each do |param|
        errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing path parameter #{param}" unless actual_params.include?(param)
      end
      # Guard the invariant restored by the $ref-query-param fix: no operation may
      # declare the same (name, in) parameter twice (e.g. a manual live override
      # plus a now-surviving $ref of the same query param).
      resolved_param_keys = Array(op["parameters"]).map do |param|
        next nil unless param.is_a?(Hash)

        ref = param["$ref"]
        comp = ref&.start_with?("#/components/parameters/") ? (components.dig("parameters", ref.split("/").last) || {}) : param
        name = comp["name"]
        name.nil? ? nil : [name, comp["in"]]
      end.compact
      param_counts = Hash.new(0)
      resolved_param_keys.each { |key| param_counts[key] += 1 }
      param_counts.each do |(dup_name, dup_in), count|
        errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} duplicate parameter #{dup_name} (#{dup_in})" if count > 1
      end
      if path.include?("/reports/") || path.include?("shared-reports")
        servers = Array(op["servers"]).map { |server| server["url"] }
        errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing reports server" unless servers.include?(REPORTS_SERVER)
      end
      if op["x-clockify-host"] == AUDIT_LOG_SERVER
        servers = Array(op["servers"]).map { |server| server["url"] }
        errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing audit-log server" unless servers.include?(AUDIT_LOG_SERVER)
      end
    end
  end
  if repo_root
    catalog_path = File.join(repo_root, "docs/tool-catalog.json")
    if File.exist?(catalog_path)
      errors.concat(catalog_contract_errors(JSON.parse(File.read(catalog_path))))
    end

    allowlist = mcp_probe_allowlist_keys(repo_root)
    if allowlist
      missing = document_operation_keys(doc, raw_allowlist_required_only: true) - allowlist
      missing.each do |operation|
        errors << "probe_lab_api allowlist missing OpenAPI operation #{operation}"
      end
    end
  end
  LAST_PAGE_HEADER_OPS.each do |(method, path)|
    unless PAGINATED_LIST_OPS.include?([method, path])
      errors << "LAST_PAGE_HEADER_OPS entry #{method.upcase} #{path} is not in PAGINATED_LIST_OPS; a last-page-header op must also be paginated"
    end
  end
  errors.concat(paginated_ops_live_evidence_errors(doc))
  errors
end

# Verify every entry in PAGINATED_LIST_OPS made it into the emitted
# spec AND is backed by live evidence — the operation must carry an
# `x-clockify-live-status` of `live-success` or `probe-documented`. The
# `documented` bucket is rejected because it means the entry was added
# without a passing live probe or a recorded probe fixture, and a fern
# generator pass that emits page+page-size on an operation we can't
# prove the live API honours is the exact regression that the
# `ensure_pagination!` annotation table is meant to prevent. Treating
# this as a generator-level error (rather than a downstream Go test)
# means a contributor who edits PAGINATED_LIST_OPS gets an immediate
# loud failure at `make gen-openapi` time instead of a silent shipped
# spec.
PAGINATED_LIVE_EVIDENCE_OK = Set.new(%w[live-success probe-documented]).freeze

def paginated_ops_live_evidence_errors(doc)
  errors = []
  paths = doc["paths"] || {}
  PAGINATED_LIST_OPS.each do |(method, path)|
    op = paths.dig(path, method)
    if op.nil?
      errors << "PAGINATED_LIST_OPS entry #{method.upcase} #{path} not emitted; remove the entry or restore the source operation"
      next
    end
    status = op["x-clockify-live-status"].to_s
    unless PAGINATED_LIVE_EVIDENCE_OK.include?(status)
      errors << "PAGINATED_LIST_OPS entry #{method.upcase} #{path} has x-clockify-live-status=#{status.empty? ? "<unset>" : status}; must be one of #{PAGINATED_LIVE_EVIDENCE_OK.to_a.join(", ")} (back the entry with a live probe captured in addons-me/fern/spec/evidence/probes/ before re-adding)"
    end
  end
  errors
end

  return nil unless schema.is_a?(Hash)

def operation_for(doc, path, method)

def append_text!(target, key, text)
  existing = target[key].to_s.strip
  return if existing.include?(text)

  target[key] = existing.empty? ? text : "#{existing}\n#{text}"
end

def append_operation_note!(op, note)
  return unless op.is_a?(Hash)

  notes = Array(op["x-clockify-notes"])
  notes << note unless notes.include?(note)

def ensure_query_parameter!(op, name, schema:, required: false, description: nil, params_components: {})
  op["parameters"] ||= []
  existing = op["parameters"].find do |param|
    next false unless param.is_a?(Hash)

    resolve_param_field(param, params_components, "in") == "query" &&
      resolve_param_field(param, params_components, "name") == name
  end
  if existing
    # The param may have survived as a $ref now that ensure_path_parameters!
    # keeps $ref query params; replace it in place with the live-authoritative
    # inline shape so the required flag / schema win without a duplicate.
    replacement = {"in" => "query", "name" => name, "required" => required, "schema" => schema}
    replacement["description"] = description if description
    op["parameters"][op["parameters"].index(existing)] = replacement
    return
  end

  param = {
    "in" => "query",
    "name" => name,
    "required" => required,
    "schema" => schema
  }
  param["description"] = description if description
  op["parameters"] << param
end

# After apply_live_overrides! rewrites a surviving $ref query param inline (the
# resolve-aware ensure_query_parameter!), the parameter component it referenced can
# be left orphaned — prune_components already ran inside merger.document. Drop any
# components/parameters entry no longer reachable by a $ref so the emitted spec
# carries no dead parameter component. Normalization-only; not merge/dedup logic.
def prune_orphan_parameters!(doc)
  params = doc.dig("components", "parameters")
  return unless params.is_a?(Hash) && !params.empty?

  refs = []
  collect = lambda do |value|
    case value
    when Hash
      refs << value["$ref"] if value["$ref"].is_a?(String)
      value.each_value { |child| collect.call(child) }
    when Array
      value.each { |child| collect.call(child) }
    end
  end
  collect.call(doc["paths"])
  collect.call(doc["components"])
  referenced = Set.new(refs)
  params.keys.each do |name|
    params.delete(name) unless referenced.include?("#/components/parameters/#{name}")
  end
end

  #   the live API (HTTP 404 + code 3000). That path now lives in
  #   PHANTOM_PATHS; the live per-user balance read is the singular
  #   `/time-off/balance/user/{userId}` (already stamped as
  #   `balances.getForUser`).
  ["post",   "/workspaces/{workspaceId}/projects/{projectId}/memberships"]                        => {group: "projects", name: "setMembers"},
  ["delete", "/workspaces/{workspaceId}/time-off/policies/{policyId}/requests/{requestId}"]       => {group: "timeOff", name: "withdraw"}
}.freeze

def stamp_sdk_method_name!(op, method, path)
  entry = SDK_METHOD_NAMES[[method.to_s, path.to_s]]
  return unless entry

  op["x-fern-sdk-group-name"] = entry[:group]
  op["x-fern-sdk-method-name"] = entry[:name]
end

# Resolve a parameter's field ("in", "name", ...) whether the parameter is
# inline or a $ref into #/components/parameters. params_components is the merged
# @components["parameters"] map (keyed by ref tail). Returns nil when it cannot
# be resolved so callers can fall back to their inline handling.
def resolve_param_field(param, params_components, field)
  return param[field] if param.is_a?(Hash) && param.key?(field)

  ref = param.is_a?(Hash) ? param["$ref"].to_s : ""
  return nil unless ref.start_with?("#/components/parameters/")

  tail = ref.split("/").last
  comp = params_components.is_a?(Hash) ? params_components[tail] : nil
  comp.is_a?(Hash) ? comp[field] : nil
end

def ensure_path_parameters!(op, path, params_components = {})
  wanted = path.scan(/\{([^}]+)\}/).flatten
  existing = Array(op["parameters"]).select do |param|
    # Keep a $ref to a NON-path parameter (query/header/cookie: start/end, page,
    # page-size, sort-order, ...). The old predicate resolved a $ref to its
    # ref-tail name, which never matches a {path} placeholder, so every $ref
    # query param was silently pruned (then GC'd by prune_components). Inline
    # params and $ref PATH params keep the original name test below.
    if param.is_a?(Hash) && param["$ref"].is_a?(String)
      resolved_in = resolve_param_field(param, params_components, "in")
      next true if resolved_in && resolved_in != "path"
    end
    name = parameter_name(param)
    name.nil? || wanted.include?(name)
  end
  seen = existing.each_with_object(Set.new) do |param, set|
    name = parameter_name(param)
    next unless name

    set << name
  end
  wanted.each do |name|
    next if seen.include?(name)

    existing << {
      "name" => name,
      "in" => "path",
      "required" => true,
      "schema" => {"type" => "string"}
    }
    seen << name
  end
  op["parameters"] = existing unless existing.empty?
end

def json_pointer_exists?(doc, ref)
  return false unless ref.start_with?("#/")

  current = doc
  ref.sub("#/", "").split("/").each do |raw|
    token = raw.gsub("~1", "/").gsub("~0", "~")
    return false unless current.is_a?(Hash) && current.key?(token)

    current = current[token]
  end
  true
end

class Merger
  attr_reader :quarantine

  def initialize(options)
    @options = options
    @operations = {}
    @components = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = {} }
    @component_hashes = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = {} }
    @quarantine = []
    @used_operation_ids = Set.new
    @aliases = Set.new
    @security_header_aliases = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = Set.new }
  end

  def add_yaml_file(path, kind)
    doc = load_yaml_file(path)
    return unless doc.is_a?(Hash)

    label = source_label(path, @options)
    domain = domain_from_path(path)
    servers = Array(doc["servers"]).map { |server| server["url"].to_s }
    security_schemes = doc.dig("components", "securitySchemes") || {}
    collect_security_aliases(security_schemes)
    ref_maps = merge_components(doc["components"] || {}, domain)
    Array(doc.dig("components", "securitySchemes")).each { |scheme| @aliases << scheme[0].to_s if scheme[0].to_s != "ApiKeyAuth" }

    paths = doc["paths"] || {}
    paths.keys.sort.each do |raw_path|
      item = paths[raw_path]
      next unless item.is_a?(Hash)

      inherited_parameters = Array(item["parameters"])
      item.keys.map(&:to_s).select { |m| METHODS.include?(m.downcase) }.sort_by { |m| METHOD_ORDER.fetch(m.downcase, 99) }.each do |method|
        op = deep_copy(item[method])
        op["parameters"] = merge_parameters(inherited_parameters, Array(op["parameters"]))
        aliases = operation_security_aliases(op, security_schemes)
        op["x-clockify-security-aliases"] = aliases unless aliases.empty?
        rewrite_refs!(op, ref_maps)
        normalize_security!(op, @aliases)
        normalized = normalize_path(raw_path)
        host = host_for(normalized, op, servers)
        add_operation(
          method.downcase,
          normalized,
          op,
          source: label,
          domain: domain,
          host: host,
          evidence: kind,
          priority: SOURCE_PRIORITIES.fetch(kind, 0)
        )
      end
    end
  rescue StandardError => e
    reason = if defined?(Psych::SyntaxError) && e.is_a?(Psych::SyntaxError)
               "invalid YAML source quarantined"
             else
               e.message.lines.first.to_s.strip.gsub(File.expand_path(path), source_label(path, @options))
             end
    @quarantine << {
      "source" => source_label(path, @options),
      "reason" => reason
    }
  end

  def add_markdown_doc(path)
    label = source_label(path, @options)
    domain = domain_from_path(path)
    method_path_from_doc(File.readlines(path, chomp: true)).each do |method, normalized|
      op = {
        "tags" => [tag_for_domain(domain)],
        "summary" => "Documented #{method.upcase} #{normalized}",
        "description" => "Operation discovered from pasted Clockify API Markdown. Schemas stay broad unless a parsed OpenAPI source or live fixture provides narrower structure.",
        "operationId" => operation_id(method, normalized, @used_operation_ids),
        "security" => [{"ApiKeyAuth" => []}, {"AddonTokenAuth" => []}],
        "responses" => {
          "default" => {
            "description" => "Documented Clockify response.",
            "content" => {
              "application/json" => {
                "schema" => {"type" => "object", "additionalProperties" => true}
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
      add_operation(
        method,
        normalized,
        op,
        source: label,
        domain: domain,
        host: host_for(normalized, op, []),
        evidence: "doc-md",
        priority: SOURCE_PRIORITIES.fetch("doc-md")
      )
    end
  end

  def apply_metadata(findings, mcp_mapping, tool_risks, tool_meta)
    @operations.each do |(method, path), record|
      op = record[:op]
      findings_for_op = Array(findings[[method, path, record[:host]]]) + Array(findings[[method, path, nil]])
      other_host_findings = findings.each_with_object([]) do |((f_method, f_path, f_host), values), out|
        next unless f_method == method && f_path == path && f_host && f_host != record[:host]

        out.concat(values)
      end
      evidence = Array(op["x-clockify-evidence"])
      source_files = Array(op["x-clockify-source-files"])
      source_live_status = op["x-clockify-live-status"].to_s
      findings_for_op.each do |finding|
        evidence << finding["bucket"]
        source_files << finding["source"]
      end
      live_status = choose_live_status(evidence, findings_for_op, [source_live_status])
      tools = Array(mcp_mapping[[method, path]]).sort
      evidence.concat(tools.flat_map { |tool| Array(tool_meta.dig(tool, "evidence")) })
      tool_statuses = tools.flat_map { |tool| Array(tool_meta.dig(tool, "statuses")) }
      live_status = choose_live_status(evidence, findings_for_op, [source_live_status] + tool_statuses)
      risk = tools.flat_map { |tool| tool_risks[tool] }.compact
      risk = Array(op["x-clockify-risk"]) if risk.empty? && Array(op["x-clockify-risk"]).any?
      risk = default_risk_for(method) if risk.empty?

      op["x-clockify-source-files"] = source_files.uniq.sort
      op["x-clockify-host"] = record[:host]
      op["x-clockify-evidence"] = evidence.uniq.sort
      op["x-clockify-live-status"] = live_status
      op["x-clockify-mcp-tools"] = tools
      op["x-clockify-risk"] = risk.uniq.sort

      raw_notes = raw_unit_notes(path)
      op["x-clockify-raw-unit-notes"] = raw_notes unless raw_notes.empty?
      notes = Array(op["x-clockify-notes"]) + quirk_notes(path, method)
      notes.concat(findings_for_op.map { |finding| finding["note"] }) if findings_for_op.any?
      notes.concat(other_host_findings.map { |finding| "Wrong-host finding not applied to live status: #{finding["note"]}" }) if other_host_findings.any?
      notes.concat(tools.flat_map { |tool| Array(tool_meta.dig(tool, "notes")) }) if tools.any?
      op["x-clockify-notes"] = notes.uniq.sort unless notes.empty?
      ensure_path_parameters!(op, path, @components["parameters"])
      normalize_op_tags!(op)
      stamp_path_param_patterns!(op)
      ensure_pagination!(op, method, path, @components["parameters"])
      stamp_last_page_header!(op, method, path)
      stamp_sdk_method_name!(op, method, path)
      op["security"] = [{"ApiKeyAuth" => []}, {"AddonTokenAuth" => []}]
      op["servers"] = [{"url" => record[:host]}] if record[:host] != MAIN_SERVER
    end
  end

  def document
    paths = {}
    @operations.keys.sort_by { |method, path| [path, METHOD_ORDER.fetch(method, 99)] }.each do |method, path|
      paths[path] ||= {}
      paths[path][method] = sort_operation(@operations[[method, path]][:op])
    end

    doc = {
      "openapi" => "3.0.3",
      "info" => {
        "title" => "Clockify Unified OpenAPI",
        "version" => "2026-05-12",
        "description" => [
          "Generated by scripts/gen-clockify-openapi from realOPENAPI, clockify-api-probe-lab, AIII/openapi.yaml, GOCLMCP coverage docs, and QA findings.",
          "Do not edit this file by hand; run `make gen-openapi` after source evidence changes.",
          "Operation vendor extensions preserve provenance, host, live status, MCP mapping, risk, raw unit notes, and known upstream quirks."
        ].join("\n")
      },
      "servers" => [
        {"url" => MAIN_SERVER, "description" => "Main Clockify API"},
        {"url" => REPORTS_SERVER, "description" => "Clockify reports and shared-reports API"},
        {"url" => AUDIT_LOG_SERVER, "description" => "Clockify audit-log API"}
      ],
      "security" => [{"ApiKeyAuth" => []}],
      "tags" => tags(paths),
      "paths" => paths,
      "components" => pruned_components(paths),
      "x-clockify-generation" => {
        "generator" => "scripts/gen-clockify-openapi",
        "sourceManifest" => @options[:source_manifest],
        "sourcePrecedence" => [
          "live/probe findings metadata",
          "realOPENAPI operation bodies",
          "probe-lab OpenAPI operation bodies",
          "probe-lab fragments/supplementary OpenAPI operation bodies",
          "AIII official-style OpenAPI export operation bodies for otherwise-missing gaps",
          "pasted DOC Markdown operation inventory",
          "GOCLMCP catalog/coverage annotations"
        ],
        "securityAliasesNormalized" => @aliases.to_a.uniq.sort - ["ApiKeyAuth", "AddonTokenAuth"],
        "securityHeaderAliasesNormalized" => security_header_aliases
      },
      # Sort by both source and reason so multiple quarantines from the
       # same source file (e.g. the 3 phantom /policies/{policyId}/requests
       # routes all hitting time-off-b.yaml) land in a deterministic
       # total order. Without the secondary key the filesystem readdir
       # ordering bleeds through and the openapi-drift gate flips between
       # macOS local + Linux CI (#137 CI repro 2026-05-25).
      "x-clockify-source-quarantine" => @quarantine.sort_by { |entry| [entry["source"], entry["reason"]] }
    }
    doc
  end

  private

  def collect_security_aliases(schemes)
    return unless schemes.is_a?(Hash)

    schemes.each do |scheme, cfg|
      canonical = case scheme.to_s
                  when "AddonKeyAuth", "MarketplaceKeyAuth"
                    @aliases << scheme.to_s
                    "AddonTokenAuth"
                  when "ApiKeyAuth"
                    "ApiKeyAuth"
                  else
                    scheme.to_s
                  end
      header = cfg.is_a?(Hash) ? cfg["name"].to_s : ""
      @security_header_aliases[canonical] << header unless header.empty?
    end
  end

  def security_header_aliases
    @security_header_aliases.keys.sort.each_with_object({}) do |scheme, out|
      out[scheme] = @security_header_aliases[scheme].to_a.sort
    end
  end

  def merge_components(components, domain)
    ref_maps = Hash.new { |h, key| h[key] = {} }
    components.each do |section, values|
      next if section.to_s == "securitySchemes"
      next unless values.is_a?(Hash)

      values.keys.sort.each do |name|
        value = deep_copy(values[name])
        normalize_security!(value, @aliases)
        hash = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(canonical_json(value))
        existing_by_hash = @component_hashes[section][hash]
        if existing_by_hash
          ref_maps[section][name] = existing_by_hash
          next
        end

        target = name
        if @components[section].key?(target)
          prefix = pascal_domain(domain)
          target = "#{prefix}#{name}"
          suffix = 2
          while @components[section].key?(target)
            target = "#{prefix}#{name}#{suffix}"
            suffix += 1
          end
        end
        @components[section][target] = value
        @component_hashes[section][hash] = target
        ref_maps[section][name] = target
      end
    end
    ref_maps.each do |section, mapping|
      mapping.each_value do |target|
        rewrite_refs!(@components[section][target], ref_maps) if @components[section][target]
      end
    end
    ref_maps
  end

  def merge_parameters(path_params, op_params)
    # NOTE: do NOT use `path_params.concat(op_params)` here — Array#concat
    # mutates the receiver in place. `path_params` is captured once per
    # path-item by the caller and reused across every operation under
    # that path; mutating it leaked the previous method's query params
    # onto the next method, producing duplicate-identifier interfaces
    # in Fern's TS SDK output for POST/PATCH operations that shared a
    # path with a GET (e.g. POST /tags inherited GET /tags's `name`
    # query param even though probe-lab's POST defined no query params).
    # The non-destructive `+` operator avoids the leak.
    merged = []
    seen = Set.new
    (path_params + op_params).each do |param|
      key = if param.is_a?(Hash) && param["$ref"]
              param["$ref"]
            elsif param.is_a?(Hash)
              "#{param["in"]}:#{param["name"]}"
            else
              param.to_s
            end
      next if seen.include?(key)

      seen << key
      merged << param
    end
    merged
  end

  def add_operation(method, path, op, source:, domain:, host:, evidence:, priority:)
    if phantom_path?(method, path)
      @quarantine << {
        "source" => source,
        "reason" => "phantom path quarantined (#{method.upcase} #{path}): see PHANTOM_PATHS in scripts/gen-clockify-openapi"
      }
      return
    end
    op = deep_copy(op)
    source_evidence = Array(op["x-clockify-evidence"])
    source_live_status = op["x-clockify-live-status"].to_s
    op["operationId"] = operation_id(method, path, @used_operation_ids) if op["operationId"].to_s.empty?
    op["tags"] = [tag_for_domain(domain)] if Array(op["tags"]).empty?
    op["x-clockify-source-files"] = [source]
    op["x-clockify-host"] = host
    op["x-clockify-evidence"] = ([evidence] + source_evidence).uniq.sort
    op["x-clockify-live-status"] = source_live_status.empty? ? (evidence == "real-openapi" ? "documented" : evidence) : source_live_status

    key = [method, path]
    existing = @operations[key]
    if existing.nil? || priority > existing[:priority]
      if existing
        op["x-clockify-source-files"] = (Array(op["x-clockify-source-files"]) + Array(existing[:op]["x-clockify-source-files"])).uniq.sort
        op["x-clockify-evidence"] = (Array(op["x-clockify-evidence"]) + Array(existing[:op]["x-clockify-evidence"])).uniq.sort
      end
      @operations[key] = {op: op, priority: priority, host: host}
    else
      existing[:op]["x-clockify-source-files"] = (Array(existing[:op]["x-clockify-source-files"]) + [source]).uniq.sort
      existing[:op]["x-clockify-evidence"] = (Array(existing[:op]["x-clockify-evidence"]) + [evidence]).uniq.sort
      existing[:host] = REPORTS_SERVER if host == REPORTS_SERVER
    end
  end

  def choose_live_status(evidence, findings, tool_statuses = [])
    buckets = findings.map { |finding| finding["bucket"] }
    buckets.concat(tool_statuses)
    return "live-success" if buckets.include?("live-success")
    return "workspace-state-limited" if buckets.include?("workspace-state-limited")
    return "permission-gated" if buckets.include?("permission-gated")
    # A wrong-verb 405 is as unsupported as an absent path for callers; the
    # separate bucket exists so evidence readers can tell the two apart.
    return "unsupported" if buckets.include?("unsupported") || buckets.include?("method-not-allowed")
    return "unit-only" if buckets.include?("unit-only")
    return "probe-documented" if evidence.any? { |entry| entry.to_s.start_with?("probe") }

    "documented"
  end

  def sort_operation(op)
    preferred = %w[tags summary description operationId servers security parameters requestBody responses]
    out = {}
    preferred.each { |key| out[key] = sort_deep(op[key]) if op.key?(key) }
    op.keys.map(&:to_s).sort.each do |key|
      next if out.key?(key)

      out[key] = sort_deep(op[key])
    end
    out
  end

  def tag_for_domain(domain)
    {
      "custom_fields" => "Custom Fields",
      "time_entries" => "Time Entries",
      "time_off" => "Time Off",
      "user_groups" => "User Groups"
    }.fetch(domain, domain.split(/[^a-z0-9]+/).map { |part| part[0].upcase + part[1..] }.join(" "))
  end

  def tags(paths)
    names = paths.values.flat_map do |item|
      item.values.flat_map { |op| Array(op["tags"]) }
    end.uniq.sort
    names.map { |name| {"name" => name} }
  end

  def pruned_components(paths)
    refs = Set.new
    collect_refs(paths, refs)
    changed = true
    while changed
      changed = false
      refs.to_a.each do |ref|
        match = ref.match(%r{\A#/components/([^/]+)/([^/]+)\z})
        next unless match

        value = @components.dig(match[1], match[2])
        next unless value

        before = refs.size
        collect_refs(value, refs)
        changed ||= refs.size > before
      end
    end

    out = {
      "securitySchemes" => {
        "ApiKeyAuth" => {"type" => "apiKey", "in" => "header", "name" => "X-Api-Key"},
        "AddonTokenAuth" => {"type" => "apiKey", "in" => "header", "name" => "X-Addon-Token"}
      }
    }
    @components.keys.sort.each do |section|
      kept = {}
      @components[section].keys.sort.each do |name|
        ref = "#/components/#{section}/#{name}"
        kept[name] = sort_deep(@components[section][name]) if refs.include?(ref)
      end
      out[section] = kept unless kept.empty?
    end
    out
  end

  def collect_refs(value, refs)
    case value
    when Hash
      refs << value["$ref"] if value["$ref"].is_a?(String)
      value.each_value { |child| collect_refs(child, refs) }
    when Array
      value.each { |child| collect_refs(child, refs) }
    end
  end
end

def raw_allowlist_required?(op)
  host = op["x-clockify-host"].to_s
  host.empty? || host == MAIN_SERVER || host == REPORTS_SERVER
end

def document_operation_keys(doc, raw_allowlist_required_only: false)
  keys = []
  (doc["paths"] || {}).each do |path, item|
    item.each do |method, op|
      next unless METHODS.include?(method)
      next if raw_allowlist_required_only && !raw_allowlist_required?(op)

      keys << "#{method.upcase} #{normalize_path(path)}"
    end
  end
  keys.uniq.sort
end

def mcp_probe_allowlist_keys(repo_root)
  path = File.join(repo_root, "internal/tools/tier2_probe_lab_api_gen.go")
  return nil unless File.exist?(path)

  verbs = {
    "Get" => "GET",
    "Post" => "POST",
    "Put" => "PUT",
    "Patch" => "PATCH",
    "Delete" => "DELETE"
  }
  File.read(path).scan(/Method:\s+http\.Method(\w+),\s+Path:\s+"([^"]+)"/m).map do |method, raw_path|
    verb = verbs.fetch(method)
    "#{verb} #{normalize_path(raw_path)}"
  end.uniq.sort
end

def validate_document(doc, repo_root = nil)
  errors = []
  paths = doc["paths"] || {}
  operation_ids = {}
  components = doc["components"] || {}
  refs = []
  collect = lambda do |value|
    case value
    when Hash
      refs << value["$ref"] if value["$ref"].is_a?(String)
      value.each_value { |child| collect.call(child) }
    when Array
      value.each { |child| collect.call(child) }
    end
  end
  collect.call(paths)
  collect.call(components)

  refs.uniq.each { |ref| errors << "unresolved ref #{ref}" if ref.start_with?("#/") && !json_pointer_exists?(doc, ref) }

  CORE_ENTITY_REQUIRED_FIELDS.each do |schema_name, fields|
    schema = components.dig("schemas", schema_name)
    if !schema.is_a?(Hash)
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} missing"
      next
    end
    props = schema["properties"]
    required = schema["required"]
    if !props.is_a?(Hash)
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} missing properties"
      next
    end
    if !required.is_a?(Array) || required.empty?
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} must declare a non-empty required[]"
      next
    end
    fields.each do |field|
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} missing property #{field}" unless props.key?(field)
      errors << "schema #{schema_name} required[] missing #{field}" unless required.include?(field)
    end
  end

  paths.each do |path, item|
    item.each do |method, op|
      next unless METHODS.include?(method)

      id = op["operationId"].to_s
      errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing operationId" if id.empty?
      errors << "duplicate operationId #{id}" if operation_ids.key?(id)
      operation_ids[id] = true
      errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing security" if Array(op["security"]).empty?
      expected_params = path.scan(/\{([^}]+)\}/).flatten
      actual_params = Array(op["parameters"]).map do |param|
        next nil unless param.is_a?(Hash)
        next param["name"] if param["in"] == "path"

        ref = param["$ref"]
        if ref&.start_with?("#/components/parameters/")
          components.dig("parameters", ref.split("/").last, "name")
        end
      end.compact
      expected_params.each do |param|
        errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing path parameter #{param}" unless actual_params.include?(param)
      end
      # Guard the invariant restored by the $ref-query-param fix: no operation may
      # declare the same (name, in) parameter twice (e.g. a manual live override
      # plus a now-surviving $ref of the same query param).
      resolved_param_keys = Array(op["parameters"]).map do |param|
        next nil unless param.is_a?(Hash)

        ref = param["$ref"]
        comp = ref&.start_with?("#/components/parameters/") ? (components.dig("parameters", ref.split("/").last) || {}) : param
        name = comp["name"]
        name.nil? ? nil : [name, comp["in"]]
      end.compact
      param_counts = Hash.new(0)
      resolved_param_keys.each { |key| param_counts[key] += 1 }
      param_counts.each do |(dup_name, dup_in), count|
        errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} duplicate parameter #{dup_name} (#{dup_in})" if count > 1
      end
      if path.include?("/reports/") || path.include?("shared-reports")
        servers = Array(op["servers"]).map { |server| server["url"] }
        errors << "#{method.upcase} #{path} missing reports server" unless servers.include?(REPORTS_SERVER)

# spec AND is backed by live evidence — the operation must carry an
# `x-clockify-live-status` of `live-success` or `probe-documented`. The
# `documented` bucket is rejected because it means the entry was added
# without a passing live probe or a recorded probe fixture, and a fern
# generator pass that emits page+page-size on an operation we can't
# prove the live API honours is the exact regression that the
# `ensure_pagination!` annotation table is meant to prevent. Treating
# this as a generator-level error (rather than a downstream Go test)
# means a contributor who edits PAGINATED_LIST_OPS gets an immediate
# loud failure at `make gen-openapi` time instead of a silent shipped

PAGINATED_LIVE_EVIDENCE_OK = Set.new(%w[live-success probe-documented]).freeze

def paginated_ops_live_evidence_errors(doc)
  errors = []
  paths = doc["paths"] || {}
  PAGINATED_LIST_OPS.each do |(method, path)|
    op = paths.dig(path, method)
    if op.nil?
      errors << "PAGINATED_LIST_OPS entry #{method.upcase} #{path} not emitted; remove the entry or restore the source operation"
      next
    end
    status = op["x-clockify-live-status"].to_s

      errors << "PAGINATED_LIST_OPS entry #{method.upcase} #{path} has x-clockify-live-status=#{status.empty? ? "<unset>" : status}; must be one of #{PAGINATED_LIVE_EVIDENCE_OK.to_a.join(", ")} (back the entry with a live probe captured in addons-me/fern/spec/evidence/probes/ before re-adding)"

  existing = target[key].to_s.strip

def ensure_query_parameter!(op, name, schema:, required: false, description: nil, params_components: {})
  op["parameters"] ||= []
  existing = op["parameters"].find do |param|
    next false unless param.is_a?(Hash)

    replacement["description"] = description if description
    op["parameters"][op["parameters"].index(existing)] = replacement

    "name" => name,

  params = doc.dig("components", "parameters")

  collect.call(doc["components"])

## Webhook delivery — signature scheme

### `webhook.signature-scheme.shared-secret-not-hmac-doc-only` — DOCUMENTED 2026-05-24

- **Official claim:** Clockify webhook delivery uses a per-webhook
  `authToken` (32-char shared secret) sent in the
  `Clockify-Signature-Token` HTTP header on every delivery.
  Verification is a constant-time string compare against the stored
  token. Two source citations:
  1. `../../../GOCLMCP/docs/openapi/sources/clockify-api-probe-lab/openapi-fragments/webhooks-a.yaml`:
     `authToken: {type: string, description: "Header value Clockify
     sends as Clockify-Signature-Token; rotate via /token endpoint."}`
  2. `../../../GOCLMCP/docs/openapi/sources/clockify-api-probe-lab/WEBHOOKDOC.md`
     line 340: `Creating a webhook generates a new token which can
     be used to verify that the webhook being sent was sent by
     Clockify, as it will always be present in the header.`
- **Actual behavior:** NOT live-probed yet. The wrapper's
  `verifyClockifyWebhook` and `constructEvent` helpers ship to
  v0.x assuming the documented scheme is accurate. They do
  case-insensitive header lookup, constant-time `Buffer` compare
  via `node:crypto.timingSafeEqual`, and pad-to-equal-length to
  avoid throwing on length mismatch.
- **Live evidence:** none yet. To probe: register a Clockify
  webhook against a test endpoint that logs all incoming headers +
  body; trigger one event; capture the request; confirm the header
  name is exactly `Clockify-Signature-Token` (or a case variant)
  and the value is the unhashed `authToken` (NOT an HMAC over the
  payload). The synced `Webhook.authToken` field docstring says
  "HMAC secret" which conflicts with the probe-lab doc's
  shared-secret-comparison model — one of the two is wrong.
- **MCP tools affected:** none — the Go MCP layer in GOCLMCP does
  not currently expose webhook verification. The wrapper's new
  `clockify-sdk-ts/webhooks` subpath is the first SDK surface that
  enforces this scheme.
- **Open questions:**
  1. Header name: exactly `Clockify-Signature-Token`? Any
     case variation (e.g. `clockify-signature-token` per HTTP
     normalization in Node)? Helpers do case-insensitive lookup so
     this is robust either way, but the canonical form should be
     confirmed.
  2. Value form: bare 32-char token (matches `authToken`) or
     prefixed (`Token <value>`, `Bearer <value>`)? Helpers assume
     bare; a prefix would make them fail-closed.
  3. HMAC-vs-shared-secret: the `Webhook.authToken` docstring
     ("HMAC secret. Treat as a credential; never log.") conflicts
     with the probe-lab doc's plain-token-comparison model.
     Resolve via a live probe; if HMAC, the verifier needs a
     full rewrite (compute HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical payload
     + compare to header).
  4. Replay protection: any timestamp header for tolerance-based
     replay rejection (Stripe-style)? Doc doesn't mention one.
- **Status:** `verifier-shipped-on-doc; live-probe-pending`. The
  wrapper's verifier ships against the documented scheme. If a
  live probe (next time someone configures a Clockify webhook
  end-to-end) shows a different scheme, this entry reopens and the
  helpers update accordingly. Until then, the documented scheme is
  the authoritative source.

## Webhook create — `name` requiredness is auth-scheme-dependent

### `webhook.create.name-required-on-api-key-not-addon` — DOCUMENTED 2026-06-22

- **Official claim:** `WebhookRequest.name` carries `minLength: 2`,
  `maxLength: 30` and sits in the schema's `required[]` (with `url`,
  `webhookEvent`, `triggerSource`, `triggerSourceType`) in
  `spec/corrected/clockify.corrected.openapi.yaml`. The published spec
  does not record that the requirement is conditional on auth scheme.
- **Actual behavior:** `name` requiredness on
  `POST /workspaces/{id}/webhooks` is **auth-scheme-dependent**
  (maintainer-confirmed 2026-06-22):
  - **API key** (user-created webhooks, `X-Api-Key`) — `name` is REQUIRED.
  - **Addon token** (addon-created webhooks) — `name` is NOT required.
  The same `required[]` over-specifies in the other direction too:
  `triggerSource` is accepted EMPTY for a workspace-scoped event (the
  2026-06-21 live probe sent `triggerSource:[]` and got 201), so
  `required[]` is not a reliable per-field oracle for this schema.
- **Live evidence:** the 2026-06-21 sandbox create→update→delete probe
  (`../../../GOCLMCP/docs/openapi/sources/clockify-api-probe-lab/findings/webhooks.md`,
  Leftovers:0) was an **API-key** call and supplied `name` — consistent
  with "required on the API-key path." A no-name API-key create was not
  separately probed; the requiredness itself is maintainer-confirmed, and
  the only auth scheme this SDK family uses is the API key.
- **MCP / CLI / SDK affected:** `clockify_webhooks_create` makes `name`
  required (`z.string().min(2).max(30)`), matching the spec field shape
  and the primary `clockify_setup_webhook` workflow (tightened 2026-06-23
  from `min(1)` to the same `min(2).max(30)`). This SDK family is API-key-only (`X-Api-Key` /
  `CLOCKIFY_API_KEY`), so the required-name path is the only one it can
  reach. Same auth-scheme-conditional shape as the wrapper's
  `mapAddonTokenRestriction(err, { authScheme })` / `AddonTokenRestrictionError`.
- **Open questions:** RESOLVED 2026-06-23 (live). A no-name **API-key**
  webhook create returns **400** (no webhook created): omitting `name` 400s
  with a misleading `{"message":"Webhook already exists","code":501}`, and an
  empty-string `name` 400s with the clean `"length must be between 2 and 30"`
  — both confirm `name` is REQUIRED (2–30 chars) on the API-key path, while a
  valid 2–30 name returns 201. A/B isolated on untouched webhook events to
  rule out duplicate-detection. Evidence: GOCLMCP
  `findings/live-promotion-2026-06-23-stragglers.md`. The addon path (where
  `name` is optional, per the official spec's `required[]`) stays unreachable
  from this API-key SDK.

  payload). The synced `Webhook.authToken` field docstring says
  "HMAC secret" which conflicts with the probe-lab doc's
  shared-secret-comparison model — one of the two is wrong.
- **MCP tools affected:** none — the Go MCP layer in GOCLMCP does
  not currently expose webhook verification. The wrapper's new
  `clockify-sdk-ts/webhooks` subpath is the first SDK surface that
  enforces this scheme.
- **Open questions:**
  1. Header name: exactly `Clockify-Signature-Token`? Any
     case variation (e.g. `clockify-signature-token` per HTTP
     normalization in Node)? Helpers do case-insensitive lookup so
     this is robust either way, but the canonical form should be
     confirmed.
  2. Value form: bare 32-char token (matches `authToken`) or
     prefixed (`Token <value>`, `Bearer <value>`)? Helpers assume
     bare; a prefix would make them fail-closed.

## Webhook create — `name` requiredness is auth-scheme-dependent

### `webhook.create.name-required-on-api-key-not-addon` — DOCUMENTED 2026-06-22

- **Official claim:** `WebhookRequest.name` carries `minLength: 2`,
  `maxLength: 30` and sits in the schema's `required[]` (with `url`,
  `webhookEvent`, `triggerSource`, `triggerSourceType`) in
  `spec/corrected/clockify.corrected.openapi.yaml`. The published spec
  does not record that the requirement is conditional on auth scheme.
- **Actual behavior:** `name` requiredness on
  `POST /workspaces/{id}/webhooks` is **auth-scheme-dependent**
  (maintainer-confirmed 2026-06-22):
  - **API key** (user-created webhooks, `X-Api-Key`) — `name` is REQUIRED.
  - **Addon token** (addon-created webhooks) — `name` is NOT required.
  The same `required[]` over-specifies in the other direction too:
  `triggerSource` is accepted EMPTY for a workspace-scoped event (the
  2026-06-21 live probe sent `triggerSource:[]` and got 201), so
  `required[]` is not a reliable per-field oracle for this schema.
- **Live evidence:** the 2026-06-21 sandbox create→update→delete probe
  (`../../../GOCLMCP/docs/openapi/sources/clockify-api-probe-lab/findings/webhooks.md`,
  Leftovers:0) was an **API-key** call and supplied `name` — consistent
  with "required on the API-key path." A no-name API-key create was not
  separately probed; the requiredness itself is maintainer-confirmed, and
  the only auth scheme this SDK family uses is the API key.
- **MCP / CLI / SDK affected:** `clockify_webhooks_create` makes `name`
  required (`z.string().min(2).max(30)`), matching the spec field shape
  and the primary `clockify_setup_webhook` workflow (tightened 2026-06-23
  from `min(1)` to the same `min(2).max(30)`). This SDK family is API-key-only (`X-Api-Key` /
  `CLOCKIFY_API_KEY`), so the required-name path is the only one it can
  reach. Same auth-scheme-conditional shape as the wrapper's
  `mapAddonTokenRestriction(err, { authScheme })` / `AddonTokenRestrictionError`.
- **Open questions:** RESOLVED 2026-06-23 (live). A no-name **API-key**
  webhook create returns **400** (no webhook created): omitting `name` 400s
  with a misleading `{"message":"Webhook already exists","code":501}`, and an
  empty-string `name` 400s with the clean `"length must be between 2 and 30"`
  — both confirm `name` is REQUIRED (2–30 chars) on the API-key path, while a
  valid 2–30 name returns 201. A/B isolated on untouched webhook events to
  rule out duplicate-detection. Evidence: GOCLMCP
  `findings/live-promotion-2026-06-23-stragglers.md`. The addon path (where
  `name` is optional, per the official spec's `required[]`) stays unreachable
  from this API-key SDK.

  corrected spec (111 → 129/184) via GOCLMCP

  billable/cost rate, user hourly/cost rate, project-user hourly/cost rate, invoice
  settings update, invoice status change (PATCH), give/remove manager role (201/204),
  remove-user-from-group, member-profile PATCH, time-off balance PATCH (204),
  entity-info created/deleted/updated (GET `?type=PROJECTS`), webhook logs (POST),

- **Actual behavior:** **404 / `No static resource` / `code:3000`**.

### `webhooks.logs.method-is-post-not-get` — RESOLVED 2026-08-04/05 (live)

- **Official claim:** `getWorkspacesWorkspaceIdWebhooksWebhookIdLogs` is a **GET** on
  `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/logs`. The corrected spec already
  carries `summary: "(DOCUMENTED BUT BROKEN) Get logs for a webhook"`, i.e. the repo
  knew the call failed but recorded it as broken rather than as the wrong verb.
- **Actual behavior:** `GET` → **405** with response header **`allow: POST`** and body
  `{"message":"Request method 'GET' is not supported","code":3000}`.
  `POST` to the same path with a fake webhook id → **400**
  `{"message":"Webhook doesn't belong to Workspace","code":501}` — the route is real
  and the 400 is the fake-id branch, so a real webhook id should yield 2xx.
  **Confirmed 2026-08-04/05**: a real webhook id via POST returns a genuine **200**
  with the log array (`{id, webhookId, statusCode, requestBody, responseBody,
  respondedAt}` rows). The corrected spec already carried a *separate*, correctly-
  shaped POST operation for the same path — `getWebhookLogs`/`searchLogs`,
  already `live-success` — because the merge keys on `[method, path]`, so the two
  verbs never collided as one operation to resolve by source priority; both
  survived as distinct operations.
- **MCP tools affected:** none today (`x-clockify-mcp-tools: []`, no `cli/src` or
  `mcp/src` reference), so this is a spec-truth defect rather than a shipped bug.
- **Open questions:** none — resolved.

  phantom wrong-verb duplicate, not a documentation gap to fix by changing its
  verb — the correct POST operation already existed and was already
  `live-success`. Quarantined
  `["get", "/workspaces/{workspaceId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/logs"]` in
  `../GOCLMCP/scripts/gen-clockify-openapi`'s `PHANTOM_PATHS` (path survives via
  the POST sibling; operation count drops by one). See the sibling
  `gen-clockify-openapi.status_bucket.405-conflated-with-phantom` entry below for
  why this was *not* hand-added as a path-level phantom.

### `gen-clockify-openapi.status_bucket.405-conflated-with-phantom` — RESOLVED 2026-08-05

- **Official claim:** N/A — sibling generator behaviour.
- **Actual behavior:** `../GOCLMCP/scripts/gen-clockify-openapi`'s `status_bucket`
  classifies a response as `unsupported` when the status is one of
  `[400, 404, 405, 409, 415, 422]` **and** the body matches
  `/no static resource|"code":\s*3000/`. Clockify returns `code:3000` for *both*
  "path not served" (404, message `No static resource …`) **and** "wrong verb on an
  existing path" (405, message `Request method 'GET' is not supported`). Because
  `405` is in the status list and the `code:3000` alternative matches on the code
  alone, a wrong-method route on a **live path** is bucketed identically to a
  genuinely absent path.
- **How it was found:** the 2026-07-28 sweep reproduced the same flaw in an
  independent classifier written from the generator's rule; `webhooks/{id}/logs`
  was labelled phantom until its `allow: POST` header was inspected.
- **Consequence (traced, not assumed):** this is a *diagnostic-precision* defect, not
  an automatic deletion. `status_bucket`'s output flows
  `finding["bucket"]` → `choose_live_status` → `x-clockify-live-status`; it does **not**
  drive quarantine, which is the hardcoded `PHANTOM_PATHS` list. A 405 also reaches
  `unsupported` through the generic `[400, 404, 405, …]` branch further down, so the
  emitted bucket is `unsupported` either way. The harm is that `unsupported` cannot
  distinguish "path absent" from "wrong verb on a live path", so a human auditing the
  evidence can mistake a live route for a phantom and hand-add it to `PHANTOM_PATHS`
  — which is exactly what nearly happened when this sweep first classified
  `webhooks/{id}/logs`.
- **Fix applied 2026-08-05 (GOCLMCP `7d26f48`):** exactly the suggested fix.
  `status_bucket` now returns a dedicated `method-not-allowed` bucket for any 405,
  tested *before* the absent-path branch, and the absent-path branch matches the
  `No static resource` **message** instead of the bare `code:3000` that Clockify
  reuses. The comment records the distinguishing wire signal, the `allow` header.
- **Why the deferral no longer applied:** the feared propagation is avoidable.
  `choose_live_status` maps buckets through a closed vocabulary, so mapping
  `method-not-allowed` to `unsupported` there leaves `x-clockify-live-status`
  untouched. Regenerating the contract produced a **byte-identical** file, so no

4:    "description": "## Introduction
By using this REST API, you can easily integrate Clockify with your own add-ons, push and pull data
between Clockify and other tools, and create custom add-ons on [CAKE.com Marketplace](https://marketplace.cake.com).
Whether you’re looking to automate time tracking, generate custom reports, or build other custom
integrations, our API provides the flexibility and power you need to get the job done. If you
have any questions or run into any issues while using our API, don’t hesitate to reach out to us for help.
You can also post questions on Stack Overflow with the Clockify tag to get help from the community.
## Authentication
To authenticate your requests to your API, make sure to include either the ‘X-Api-Key’ or the
‘X-Addon-Token’ in the request header, containing your API or Addon key. If your workspace is
on a subdomain (e.g. subdomain.clockify.me), you’ll need to generate a new API key in your
Profile Settings that will work specifically for that workspace. This ensures that you’re
accessing data from the correct workspace and helps maintain the security of your data.
## Webhooks
Webhooks can enhance your workflow by keeping your add-on up-to-date with the latest changes in
Clockify. With Clockify’s webhooks you can receive real-time notifications when certain events such as
starting a timer or deleting a time entry occur in Clockify.
Depending on the workspace plan, workspace owners and admins can create:

* Up to 3 webhooks on **FREE** plan
* Up to 10 webhooks per user, with a total of 100 webhooks per entire workspace
on **BASIC**, **STANDARD** and **PRO** plans
* Up to 100 webhooks per user, with a total of 300 webhooks per entire workspace on **ENTERPRISE** plan

## Rate limiting
Our REST API has a specific rate limit of 50 requests per second (by addon on one workspace) when
accessed using X-Addon-Token. Exceeding this limit will result in an error message with the description
"Too many requests".
## Pagination
Our REST API supports pagination for all synchronous GET endpoints that retrieve lists of entities.
When an endpoint accepts the `page` and `pageSize` query parameters, it will return a paginated response.

To control the data returned in a paginated request, you can use the following optional query parameters.

- **page** (integer): The page number you wish to retrieve. This is 1-indexed. If this parameter is omitted,
the API will default to the first page (page=1).
- **pageSize** (integer): The number of items to include on each page. If this parameter is omitted,
a default page size will be used.

Every response from an endpoint that supports these parameters will include a custom `Last-Page` header.
This header provides a simple way to determine if you have reached the end of the data set.

- **true:** The current page is the final page; no more data is available.
- **false:** Additional pages can be fetched.
## API URLs
Refer to the list on what URL to use base on the subdomain and data region settings of your workspace.
* Global - can be used by workspaces with or without subdomain.
    * Regular: https://api.clockify.me/api/v1/file/image
    * Reports: https://reports.api.clockify.me/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/reports/detailed
* Regional
    * Non-subdomain
        * Regular: https://euc1.clockify.me/api/v1/file/image
        * Reports: https://use2.clockify.me/report/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/reports/detailed
    * Subdomain
        * Regular: https://euc1.clockify.me/api/v1/file/image
        * Reports: https://yoursubdomainname.clockify.me/report/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/reports/detailed
* Developer
    * Regular: https://developer.clockify.me/api/v1/file/image
    * Reports: https://developer.clockify.me/report/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/reports/detailed
## Regional Server Prefixes
If your workspace is in a specific region, you need to change your URL prefix to access v1 API endpoints.
For example, this is how **backend** api [v1/file/image](#tag/User/operation/uploadImage) endpoint
would look in EU region:
[https://euc1.clockify.me/api/v1/file/image](https://euc1.clockify.me)

Below are the available regional server prefixes:
* **EU (Germany)**: euc1
* **USA**: use2
* **UK**: euw2
* **AU**: apse2


## Breaking changes
Breaking changes in APIs are modifications that disrupt existing integrations,
requiring users to update their applications to maintain functionality.
These changes can lead to failures or unexpected results if not addressed.
See the list of [breaking changes](breaking-changes/).

## Experimental APIs
The experimental API has been thoroughly tested and is ready for use in production. However, please note that user feedback may lead to changes in the API’s structure or functionality. If you choose to use the experimental API, be prepared to modify your application code accordingly to accommodate any updates.",

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Webhooks live probe — DSAUDIT_ prefixed, sacrificial workspace.
# Never prints the API key or webhook authTokens.
set -u
source /tmp/clockify-openapi-audit/env.sh
BASE="https://api.clockify.me/api/v1"
WS="$CLOCKIFY_WORKSPACE_ID"
AUTH="X-Api-Key: $CLOCKIFY_API_KEY"
HDRS=(-H "$AUTH" -H "Content-Type: application/json")

req() { # req <label> <method> <path> [body]
  local label="$1" method="$2" path="$3" body="${4:-}"
  local code
  local tmp=$(mktemp)
  local hdr=$(mktemp)
  if [ -n "$body" ]; then
    code=$(curl -s -o "$tmp" -D "$hdr" -w "%{http_code}" -X "$method" "${HDRS[@]}" -d "$body" "$BASE$path")
  else
    code=$(curl -s -o "$tmp" -D "$hdr" -w "%{http_code}" -X "$method" "${HDRS[@]}" "$BASE$path")
  fi
  local allow=$(grep -i "^allow:" "$hdr" | tr -d '\r' | sed 's/^[Aa]llow: //I')
  echo "=== $label"
  echo "    $method $path -> HTTP $code${allow:+ | Allow: $allow}"
  # print body but redact authToken values
  if [ -s "$tmp" ]; then
    sed -E 's/("authToken"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*")[^"]+/\1<REDACTED>/g' "$tmp" | head -c 900
    echo
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp" "$hdr"
  # stash status for caller
  echo "$code" > /tmp/clockify-openapi-audit/.last_code
}

req "LIST" GET "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks"

echo "## 2. CREATE without name (API-key) — expect 400"

echo
echo "## 3. CREATE with name + callbackUrl — expect 201"
CB="https://example.com/dsaudit-cb-$RANDOM"
CREATE_BODY=$(printf '{"name":"DSAUDIT probe wh %s","url":"%s","webhookEvent":"NEW_PROJECT","triggerSource":[],"triggerSourceType":"WORKSPACE_ID"}' "$RANDOM" "$CB")

  echo "## 4. GET back the created webhook"
  req "GET-ONE" GET "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/$WH_ID"

  echo
  echo "## 5. GET /webhooks/{id}/logs — expect 405 + Allow: POST"
  req "LOGS-GET" GET "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/$WH_ID/logs"

  echo
  echo "## 6a. POST /webhooks/{id}/logs (REAL id) — expect 200 log array"
  req "LOGS-POST-REAL" POST "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/$WH_ID/logs" '{"from":"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2030-01-01T00:00:00Z","status":"ALL","sortByNewest":false}'

  echo
  echo "## 6b. POST /webhooks/{id}/logs (FAKE id) — expect 400"
  req "LOGS-POST-FAKE" POST "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/000000000000000000000000/logs" '{"from":"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2030-01-01T00:00:00Z","status":"ALL","sortByNewest":false}'

  echo
  echo "## 7. PATCH /webhooks/{id}/generateNewToken (REAL id) — expect 404"
  req "GEN-NEW-TOKEN" PATCH "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/$WH_ID/generateNewToken"

  echo
  echo "## 8a. PATCH /webhooks/{id}/token (FAKE id) — expect 400 (route exists)"
  req "TOKEN-FAKE" PATCH "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/000000000000000000000000/token"

  echo
  echo "## 8b. PATCH /webhooks/{id}/token (REAL id) — expect 200 (status only, token redacted)"
  req "TOKEN-REAL" PATCH "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/$WH_ID/token"

  echo
  echo "## 9. GET /webhooks/{id}/statuses (REAL id) — expect 200"
  req "STATUSES" GET "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/$WH_ID/statuses"

  echo
  echo "## 10. Probe POST /webhooks/{id}/test — expect 404/405 (no upstream endpoint)"
  req "TEST-PROBE" POST "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/$WH_ID/test"

  echo
  echo "## 11. CLEANUP — DELETE /webhooks/{id}"
  req "DELETE" DELETE "/workspaces/$WS/webhooks/$WH_ID"
fi
echo
echo "DONE"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/clockify-openapi-audit/probe-webhooks.sh && bash /tmp/clockify-openapi-audit/probe-webhooks.sh 2>&1
